For years, it has lived up to be THE BEST multiplayer shooter.

I played this game for hundreds of hours on different platforms – on PS4, Steam Deck, and PC. I have also seen various states of this game, as I played a lot since the first seasons, with large gaps.

There is a lot of good about this game, from movement to shooting and maps, but I believe that the biggest appeal of this game is that it is focused on tactics more than on skill and reaction.

All modern shooters are skill-obsessed, and while I enjoyed playing CS and MW3 in school, now as a person with a real life and job, I can't compete with young nolifers that added headshots & slurs to the list of their primal reflexes like eating, sleeping, and toilet.

This game instead has a very large TTK, making instant kills impossible, turning each combat into a stressful chase where winning requires not only shooting, but properly utilizing movement, ults, grenades, and teamwork.

This also enables you to take bold movements, creating tight situations that will stick in your mind. Like all these shooter edits are always about shooting and multi-kills. In this game my are me hiding in plain sight while whole team seeks me and winning a match, or saving a whole team amidst a multi-squad shootout in a tight corridor.

Okay, so where do I even start? I’d say this game is kinda mid, but it can be fun to play with friends. I don't really dive deep into it or keep up with the lore since my buddies kind of dragged me into it. They said they were not forcing me, but honestly, they were pretty pushy since they’re always playing Apex Legends, and I’m not really a fan of battle royale games. 

When I first started playing this a while back, I think I was in junior or senior year of high school. I got my first win pretty easily with randoms. I was playing as Life Support, mainly just healing my teammates. But then my friends who actually love this game came around, and I wasn’t too thrilled about it. Like, I didn’t get into battle royales until Fortnite or PUBG, and I quickly noticed that no matter how casual it feels, there’s always that sweaty squad that totally ruins the vibe. 

The game is still fun, though. The maps are chill, and the weapons are okay, but I usually stick to snipers or shotguns since they can take someone out in one hit, especially when everyone’s rushing around with all that Call of Duty movement like crouching and sliding. 

What I enjoy most are the ultimate abilities. There have been some awesome clutch moments, like that time I saved my friends from an airstrike by popping my shield with Life Support. I healed them up with my little robot buddy and we actually pulled off a win, best 2 am night ever! 

Overall, the community is pretty relaxed, and the gameplay isn’t terrible. I still think the game is mid, though not the best I’ve played, but I wouldn’t totally write it off. I’d still recommend it just for fun. The only downside for me is the microtransactions; they're such a rip-off and feel like they’re just out to take your money. It’s like with other free-to-play games that want to suck cash for no good reason. The only thing I ever spent money on was the cyberpunk collab because I wanted female V for Life Support; she’s the only character I really play as.

Best FPS game out there, but...

...♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Respawn, what happened?

Apex has some of the best gunplay, movement, legends, and overall gameplay ever put into an FPS. That’s what makes the current state of the game so damn frustrating. You’ve built an incredible game and then seemingly made it your personal mission to let everything surrounding that game rot.

Every season, we hear about how you’re “working on” the cheating problem. Every season, somehow, it gets worse.

Cheaters are everywhere. Boosters are everywhere. People openly manipulating ranked games, farming badges, boosting accounts and abusing whatever exploit they can find. And the most insulting part? It feels like some of these people have been doing it for so long that they’ve basically become part of the ecosystem.

And let’s talk about boosters.

Boosting has become so normalized that it’s hard not to wonder whether Respawn actually has any incentive to kill it off. Boosters mean more accounts, more purchases, more battle passes, more cosmetics, and more money flowing through the game. Meanwhile, legitimate players get to spend their evenings fighting people who somehow have Predator-level aim while playing like they have a second set of hands.

You tell us you’re banning cheaters.

We hear it every season.

“Anti-cheat improvements.”
“Enforcement waves.”
“We’re addressing the issue.”
“We’re taking cheating seriously.”

And then you queue into ranked and discover that apparently the “enforcement wave” was a gentle breeze.

The community isn't asking for perfection. Nobody expects you to magically eliminate every cheater on Earth. But when the same problems keep coming back season after season, eventually “we’re working on it” stops sounding like an explanation and starts sounding like a loading-screen tip.

The worst part is that Apex itself is still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible. That’s why people are so angry. If the game were bad, people would just leave. Instead, we keep coming back because when Apex works, there genuinely isn't much else like it.

The movement feels incredible.
The gunplay feels incredible.
The legends are unique.
The fights can be some of the most intense moments in any FPS.

And then you lose a ranked game to someone blatantly cheating and you're left wondering why you just voluntarily subjected yourself to that experience.

Apex doesn't need another shiny cosmetic, another overpriced heirloom event, or another “we're aware of the issue” statement.

It needs its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ house cleaned.

Fix the cheating.
Fix boosting.
Actually punish repeat offenders.
Stop letting ranked integrity become a joke.
And most importantly, make players believe that the people ruining the game are actually being dealt with.

Because right now, Apex feels like the best FPS game ever created being held hostage by the worst parts of its own community.

10/10 gameplay.
1/10 management.
-10/10 anti-cheat confidence.

Would recommend the game to anyone.

Would absolutely not recommend believing Respawn when they say, “We're working on it.”
